messages:

Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Observed throughput variance vs. your demo — urgent clarification

Hi Irene,

Quick note after our internal follow-up: during our peak window last Friday we saw 25-30% lower throughput on the Redwoods endpoint vs. the demonstration metrics you shared. We have a bakeoff scheduled next week with RivalAI and need to understand whether the variance is due to our prompt patterns, a config mismatch, or model variant selection.

Two asks:
- Can you run a short stress/throughput probe against our representative workload (I attached a small sample of logs)?
- Can Redwood propose a short-term term bridge (2 months) for additional capacity at preserved pricing while we finish the bakeoff? Procurement needs language for internal approvals.

We like Redwood overall but if the bakeoff shows consistent headroom for the competitor we'll need to present that to execs.

Thanks — appreciate a quick response this week.

— Sarah
CTO, Millstone

Attachments:
- millstone-kpi-sample-logs.csv (attachment)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@millstone.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Observed throughput variance vs. your demo — urgent clarification

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context and for sending the logs. Sorry to hear you hit that during peak. We will run a targeted probe against the workload pattern you shared and report back with concrete delta drivers (prompt length, sequence distribution, batching patterns, model variant).

Proposed immediate steps:
1) Marcus will run a matched-throughput probe against your sample workload today and baseline against the demo config.
2) We’ll share a short report (latency/throughput by token length bucket, batching utilization, and KV cache hit rates) by EOD Monday.
3) Ben and I can draft a 2-month term-bridge proposal that preserves current unit pricing but adds an agreed burst pool for peak hours — we’ll include clear rollback language if bakeoff results differ.

Can you confirm whether the bakeoff environment will use your on-prem agent or the hosted API? That will affect kernel selection and quantization parity.

I’ll loop in Laura from our procurement team for legal/PO language once we have mutual terms.

Best,
Irene
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah@millstone.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T14:48:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Observed throughput variance vs. your demo — urgent clarification

Thanks — I kicked off a matched workload probe immediately using the CSV Sarah uploaded. Initial findings (quick summary):
- Baseline demo used gptx-3.1-pro (quantized, 8-bit) with batching window tuned for 120ms latency target.
- Millstone sample has a higher median prompt length (~420 tokens vs demo 260) and a larger % of turn-level function calls which creates extra KV cache churn. Those two explain ~18-22% of the throughput gap.
- I’m attaching a short PDF with token-bucket throughput by sequence length. Also: we observed an ops-level misconfiguration on Millstone’s test harness that limited concurrent streams to 80 vs the 110 we used in demo. Fixing the harness concurrency on your side + switching to the gptx-3.1-pro+kv-optim compile reduces gap to ~6-8%.

Quick fixes we recommend (non-invasive):
- Increase client-side concurrency limit to 110 (config change)
- Use the kv-optim compile path (no model change) for the bakeoff runs
- Enable prefix-KV caching for repeated conversation threads (adds ~10% throughput in our tests)

I’ll run a follow-up probe after you confirm the harness tweak.

Attachments:
- redwood-thruput-summary-20261122.pdf (attachment)

— Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@millstone.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@millstone.ai>, Millstone Procurement <procurement@millstone.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Observed throughput variance vs. your demo — urgent clarification

Thanks Marcus — we pushed the concurrency change into our staging harness and re-ran a subset of tests. Latency stayed within bounds and throughput improved ~9% on average. We can flip kv-optim and prefix-KV for the bakeoff.

Procurement: Sarah has asked for draft language on a 60-day term bridge that keeps current unit pricing and adds a defined burst pool of 50k tokens/day for Nov–Dec. Is that something Redwood can provide in a short-form amendment so we can route internally?

— Alex
Engineering Lead, Millstone
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@millstone.ai>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah@millstone.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Observed throughput variance vs. your demo — urgent clarification

Alex/Team — we can do the 60-day term bridge as a short amendment. Key points we propose:
- Preserve existing per-token unit price for 60 days (Nov 23–Jan 22).
- Add one-time allocation of 50,000 burst tokens/day during that window. Excess usage billed at standard overage rates.
- No change to data handling or security terms.
- If bakeoff shows >8% sustained performance delta vs. your chosen comparator for >=72 hours during the bridge, Millstone may request a one-time credit equal to 25% of November usage (capped at $75k).

I’ve attached a draft short-form amendment and will have legal help from Laura if you want redlines. If that structure looks good we can start DocuSign routing today.

Attachments:
- term-bridge-draft-v1.docx (attachment)

— Ben
